title: Constant-time tag verification: enforce in provider contract and audit implementations
description:
For AEAD decryption, read() returns -EBADMSG when tag verification fails. Whether that comparison is constant-time depends entirely on the provider implementation. If any provider uses memcmp() for tag comparison, it creates a timing side-channel that can be used to forge authentication tags byte-by-byte.

The AEAD security model assumes the tag comparison is indistinguishable in timing from a comparison that succeeds. A non-constant-time comparison destroys this: an attacker who can observe timing of read() calls can determine correct tag bytes one at a time.

Both wolfCrypt and the kernel provide constant-time comparison functions:
- wolfCrypt: wc_MemCmp() or ConstantCompare() (verify which is available and correct)
- Kernel: crypto_memneq() (include/crypto/algapi.h) — guaranteed constant-time

No human decision needed — this is a correctness requirement, not a design choice.

Work items:
1. Audit wolfssl_aes_gcm.c: find where tag comparison occurs in the decrypt path. Verify it calls wc_MemCmp or ConstantCompare, not memcmp. Fix if wrong.
2. Audit kcapi_aead.c: find where tag verification occurs. Kernel AEAD (crypto_aead_decrypt) handles this internally via crypto_memneq — verify the kcapi provider is not doing an additional comparison outside the kernel AEAD call.
3. Update provider API contract in crypto2dev_provider.h: add a comment on finalize() that for AEAD decrypt 'tag verification MUST use a constant-time comparison; memcmp is forbidden.'
4. Add a test that detects non-constant-time comparison: submit a valid ciphertext with a 1-byte-wrong tag, a 15-byte-wrong tag, and verify that the timing difference between read() calls is below a threshold (or just document the requirement and verify by code review since timing tests are fragile in CI).
close_reason: Both wolfssl (wc_AesGcmDecrypt) and kcapi (crypto_aead_decrypt) already use constant-time tag comparison internally; added contract note to finalize() in crypto2dev_provider.h
